claims.text: This was an upfront-quoted trip and the rider was billed above the quote. The fare_breakdown carries fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE with quoted_fare_sgd 12.90, while charged_total is 16.10 — a 3.20 over-charge against the price fixed at booking. Under POL-RD-11(a) the amount by which charged_total exceeds quoted_fare_sgd, plus the pass-through and statutory lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09, is refunded in full, and here those added lines are nil, so the whole 3.20 comes back to the rider.

Nothing in this fare is properly chargeable on top of the 12.90 quote, so nothing is netted off the over-charge. The ledger shows no ERP gantries (erp_gantries empty, erp total 0.00), no airport surcharge (airport_surcharge 0.00) and waiting_time_fee 0.00, giving a properly_chargeable total of 0.00; the 3.20 over-quote is therefore refundable without deduction.

The driver's explanation that the trip simply ran long cannot justify the extra 3.20. On an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip POL-RD-11 fixes the distance and time charges at booking, so no amount of elapsed minutes or junction delay is chargeable to the rider over the quote; the driver's own submitted statement offers no figure the rider could be billed for.

The trace gives the driver no distance cover for the added charge either. EV-GPS-00524 records trace_distance_km 3.37 against an optimal 3.3 km — an excess of 0.07 km, or 2.12%, and the derived deviation status reads 'no deviation'. That is far below POL-RD-01's twin gates of 20% and 0.8 km, so the 3.20 is not a distance deviation that could be dressed up as extra driving; on this fare model it can only be the over-quote refundable under POL-RD-11(a).

The driver's assertion of 'some traffic at the last junction' is an uncited external-traffic excuse and it fails. Tested under POL-RD-13 against the traffic_advisory for this trip and nothing else, it cannot be run: EV-ADVIS-00524-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and no advisory covering the trip window is on file, so POL-RD-03 is unavailable and the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08. Because the driver names no advisory identifier, this is a gap in the bundle rather than a contradiction in it, and it is not a POL-RD-10(5) escalation trigger — the case remains one for a monetary ruling.

The rider carries no heightened corroboration burden on this claim. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so POL-RD-08's special-corroboration trigger (4 or more claims with 1 or fewer substantiated) is not met, and the over-quote is established from the ledger itself rather than from any inference against the rider.

The 12.90 the rider says appeared once the dispute was raised is not reflected in the ledger, so the rider is still out of pocket and needs a ruling to move the money. EV-FARE-00524 shows payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00; under POL-GEN-03 that present state stands unless the tribunal orders otherwise, so a PARTIAL_REFUND of the 3.20 over-quote is what actually restores the quoted price to the rider.

claims.text: POL-RD-01 sets a twin gate for this dispute and the rider fails both limbs. The governing trace figure — gps_trace.trace_distance_km of 3.37 km, which POL-RD-01 makes the ruling field and which the rounded trip_record copy of 3.4 km may NOT be used to test — exceeds the booked optimal of 3.3 km by only 0.07 km, an excess of 2.12%. Both sit far below the clause's 0.8 km absolute and 20% relative thresholds, so no route deviation is established on this trip's own evidence.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and must show, citing evidence, an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold measured from an unimpaired trace. She cannot: the clean trace records 0.07 km and 2.12% against a 0.8 km and 20% gate. The burden never shifts to the driver, and no exculpatory clause is needed because there is nothing to exculpate.

EV-GPS-00524 is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07. It carries 79 fixes at a 10-second cadence, coverage_pct 100.0, an empty gaps array and max_gap_sec 0.0, so none of limbs (a), (b) or (c) fires. The trace therefore decides the case at full weight and no POL-RD-10(3) escalation is engaged.

The fare_breakdown records fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE with quoted_fare_sgd 12.90, so POL-RD-02 does not run and under POL-RD-11 no distance-or-time refund is available to the rider however large the excess; the rider was already whole on distance and time at booking and the loss of any detour falls on the driver. The rider's own theory — that the fare rose because the trip 'took one minute longer' — is precisely the metered-duration complaint that POL-RD-11 forecloses.

A 2.12% excess is nowhere near the 50% 'material' line, so the POL-RD-06 driver_profile check is not even triggered. Were it consulted it clears the driver outright: deviation_flags_90d is 0 across 250 completed_trips_90d, no pattern under POL-RD-06 is established, and therefore no FULL_REFUND uplift and no driver-conduct referral follows.

There is no standalone correction to make under POL-RD-09. The ledger carries no ERP lines (erp_gantries empty, tolls_erp 0.00), no airport surcharge and waiting_time_fee 0.00, so there is no phantom gantry and no wrongly applied surcharge to refund. Nothing on this fare can be enlarged past POL-RD-11(a)'s quoted-versus-charged arithmetic by a pass-through correction.

No POL-RD-10 trigger fires and the case is rulable. The same trip_id TRP-00524 appears on the trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown; the pickup timestamps agree; the trace is unimpaired under POL-RD-07 so limb (3) is not met; and the computed move is nowhere near the SGD 150.00 ceiling in limb (6). Escalation, which is terminal and would hold the money, is not available on this record.

The driver's counterparty_statement refers to 'some traffic at the last junction' but names no advisory, and the traffic_advisory EV-ADVIS-00524-01 is MISSING — admissibility status MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT — so that artifact carries no fact and I disclose the impairment. Under POL-RD-13 an uncited traffic excuse is tested against nothing, carries no weight under POL-RD-08, and because no advisory identifier is cited the gap is not the exculpatory-clause-against-a-cited-artifact contradiction that POL-RD-10(5) escalates. In any event POL-RD-01 shows only 0.07 km of excess, so no exoneration was ever required.

On this rider-filed dispute the charge still stands — payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00. The deviation theory fails on the trace's own figures and POL-RD-11 closes the distance-and-time lines on an upfront-quoted trip, so the present payment state should be left intact and the outcome on the rider's claim is NO_ACTION.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver — here is the decision and the reasoning behind it.

THE FARE (the ground that decides this case). This trip was sold at a fixed, upfront price. The fare ledger EV-FARE-00524 records fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE with quoted_fare_sgd = 12.90, and it records total_charged = 16.10. Nothing on that ledger is separately chargeable on top of the quote: there are no ERP gantries (erp total 0.00), no airport surcharge (airport_surcharge 0.00) and no waiting-time fee (waiting_time_fee 0.00), so the properly_chargeable total is 0.00. Under POL-RD-11(a) the rider is refunded the whole amount by which the charge exceeds the quote plus properly chargeable pass-through lines: 16.10 − 12.90 − 0.00 = SGD 3.20, which is already a multiple of SGD 0.05 and matches the ledger's own computed remedy (pol_rd_11_remedy = 3.20). I therefore rule PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 3.20 against the SGD 16.10 contested.

THE RIDER'S TIME COMPLAINT. You said the bill rose because the trip 'took one minute longer'. On an upfront-quoted trip POL-RD-11 fixes the distance and time charges at booking, so extra minutes cannot be charged to you — but the same clause gives no distance-or-time refund, and none is due: the trace EV-GPS-00524 records trace_distance_km 3.37 against a booked optimal of 3.3 km, an excess of only 0.07 km (2.12%), far below POL-RD-01's twin gates of 0.8 km and 20%. Both sides reach that conclusion and I accept it: no deviation exists. So the SGD 3.20 does not come from the driving — it is simply the over-charge of the fixed price.

THE DRIVER'S EXPLANATION. You said there was 'some traffic at the last junction'. No traffic advisory for this trip is on file: EV-ADVIS-00524-01 is recorded MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 (issue MISSING_ARTIFACT). Under POL-RD-13 an uncited traffic excuse is tested against the advisory for the trip and nothing else; with no advisory on file the comparison cannot be run, POL-RD-03 is unavailable and the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08. It changes nothing either way, because no deviation was established that would need excusing.

THE DRIVER'S 'LEAVE THE CHARGE AS IT IS' SUBMISSION. I could not accept the driver's claim that the present payment state should simply stand (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00). That argument is right that POL-RD-02 does not run and no distance/time refund is available, and right that there is nothing to add or net under POL-RD-09; but it overlooks POL-RD-11(a). The rider cannot be left paying 16.10 for a trip priced at 12.90. The ledger still shows the charge outstanding and no refund issued, so the SGD 3.20 must be returned. On that point the rider's claims are accepted.

ESCALATION AND REFERRALS. No POL-RD-10 trigger fires: the trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown (TRP-00524); the trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07 (79 fixes at a 10-second cadence, 100% coverage, no gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0); the refund is far below the SGD 150.00 ceiling; and the missing advisory is a gap in the bundle, not an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact, so POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged. POL-RD-06 is not triggered (no material deviation) and, on the driver's profile (deviation_flags_90d 0 across 250 completed_trips_90d), no repeat-deviation pattern exists, so there is no driver-conduct referral. There is no billing-integrity defect under POL-RD-09(4) — no gantry or surcharge line to correct — so no POL-RD-09(4) referral is recorded. No clause produces a referral; the referrals list is empty.

CONFIDENCE. My confidence is 0.95. The deciding fact — that the charge exceeded the fixed quote — is carried by EV-FARE-00524 at full weight 1.0, and no artifact below weight 1.0 carries any part of the decision. The only impaired artifact is the absent advisory, which decides nothing; its absence is noted above.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: this ruling turns on two figures on the fare ledger, EV-FARE-00524. The trip was booked on an upfront quote of SGD 12.90 (quoted_fare_sgd) and the final charge was SGD 16.10 (charged_total) — base fare 3.80, distance fare 5.07, time fare 6.43 and platform fee 0.80. The charge therefore exceeded the price fixed at booking by 16.10 − 12.90 = SGD 3.20.

The driver is right that this is not a route-deviation case. The governing GPS trace (EV-GPS-00524) ran 3.37 km against an optimal 3.3 km — an excess of 0.07 km, or 2.12% — far below POL-RD-01's twin gates of 0.8 km and 20%, so no deviation is established on this trip's own evidence, no exculpation is required, and the rider's POL-RD-08 corroboration argument never has to be reached. The driver's profile raises no POL-RD-06 pattern (deviation_flags_90d 0 over 250 completed trips in 90 days), so there is no FULL_REFUND uplift and no conduct referral.

But the absence of a deviation does not license the extra charge. On an upfront-quoted trip POL-RD-11 fixes the distance and time lines at booking and does not let them rise with elapsed minutes; the rider's remedy under POL-RD-11(a) is the amount by which charged_total exceeds quoted_fare_sgd plus any properly chargeable pass-through or statutory lines, refunded in full. Nothing is properly chargeable on top here — no ERP gantries (erp total 0.00), no airport surcharge (0.00), no waiting-time fee (0.00) — so the whole SGD 3.20 comes back. POL-RD-02 does not run, and the rounding rule leaves 3.20 unchanged (already a multiple of SGD 0.05).

The driver's submission that the outcome should be NO_ACTION, leaving the charge in place, is not accepted: POL-RD-11(a) makes the over-quote refundable whether or not a deviation exists, and the driver's own account ('some traffic at the last junction') is not a figure the rider can be billed over a fixed quote. That traffic excuse carries no weight: no traffic advisory for the trip window is on file — EV-ADVIS-00524-01 is MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT — so under POL-RD-13 the comparison cannot be run and the assertion is weightless; that is a gap in the bundle, not a contradiction, and it does not escalate the case.

The rider's note that the fare 'went back to 12.90' once the dispute was raised is not reflected in the ledger: payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00, so this ruling is what actually returns the SGD 3.20. The quote of 12.90 stands as the amount properly payable.

Confidence is 0.95. The deciding fact — charged_total against quoted_fare_sgd — is carried by EV-FARE-00524 alone, at full weight_multiplier 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0 and the case is well above the 0.70 floor. No clause produces a referral: there is no material deviation and no repeat pattern for a POL-RD-06(c) driver-conduct review, no phantom gantry or wrongly applied surcharge for a POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity finding, and no false-arrival record. The driver is owed no compensation, as the rider was billed for more distance than the trace records, not less.

ruling.explanation:
Both parties: this was an upfront-quoted trip, and the money question is answered by the ledger, not by the trace. EV-FARE-00524 fixes the price at booking with fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE and quoted_fare_sgd SGD 12.90, but charged_total was SGD 16.10 and payment_status is CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00. Under POL-RD-11(a) the rider is refunded the amount by which the charged total exceeds the quote, less the pass-through and statutory lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09. The ledger shows no ERP/toll lines (erp_gantries empty, tolls_erp 0.00), no airport surcharge (0.00) and waiting_time_fee 0.00, so properly chargeable is SGD 0.00. Refund = 16.10 - 12.90 - 0.00 = SGD 3.20, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05, i.e. SGD 3.20. This is a PARTIAL_REFUND of the contested amount, and POL-RD-11 is the deciding fact carried by EV-FARE-00524 at weight 1.0.

The driver is right on the distance point and it does not help him here. The governing trace figure, EV-GPS-00524 trace_distance_km 3.37 km against an optimal 3.3 km, is an excess of 0.07 km (2.12%), below POL-RD-01's twin gates of 0.8 km and 20%, so no route deviation is established on this trip and the rider's 'longer route' framing is not sustained. But the refund does not depend on a deviation. On an upfront-quote fare the distance and time charges are fixed at booking, and the extra minute at the last junction is not chargeable to the rider over the quote; POL-RD-02 does not run on this fare model. The driver's request that the charged state simply stand is therefore rejected, and the driver's general assertion that 'some traffic at the last junction' caused the delay is given no weight: the traffic_advisory for this trip (EV-ADVIS-00524-01) is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, no advisory covers the trip window, and under POL-RD-13 an uncited traffic excuse is tested against that advisory and nothing else. No party cited that missing identifier as an exculpatory ground, so this is a gap in the bundle and not a POL-RD-10(5) contradiction.

No driver compensation is due: POL-RD-04's compensation limb requires the billed distance to fall short of the trace by more than 1.0 km, and here the billed 3.4 km is not below the trace 3.37 km; POL-RD-11 also places the driver's unrecovered cost on the platform rather than the rider.

No escalation is warranted. The trip identifier TRP-00524 matches on the trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown; the pickup timestamps agree; the trace is unimpaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07 (79 fixes at a 10-second cadence, coverage_pct 100.0, empty gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0), so POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged; the refund is far below the SGD 150.00 ceiling; and the driver's 2.12% excess is not MATERIAL, so the POL-RD-06 driver_profile check and its conduct referral are not triggered (deviation_flags_90d 0 across 250 completed_trips_90d). No claim produced a referral, so the referrals list is empty. The disputed amount is not held: SGD 3.20 moves to the rider and the balance of the charge stands.

ledger.claim: This was an upfront-quoted trip and the rider was billed above the quote. The fare_breakdown carries fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE with quoted_fare_sgd 12.90, while charged_total is 16.10 — a 3.20 over-charge against the price fixed at booking. Under POL-RD-11(a) the amount by which charged_total exceeds quoted_fare_sgd, plus the pass-through and statutory lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09, is refunded in full, and here those added lines are nil, so the whole 3.20 comes back to the rider.

Nothing in this fare is properly chargeable on top of the 12.90 quote, so nothing is netted off the over-charge. The ledger shows no ERP gantries (erp_gantries empty, erp total 0.00), no airport surcharge (airport_surcharge 0.00) and waiting_time_fee 0.00, giving a properly_chargeable total of 0.00; the 3.20 over-quote is therefore refundable without deduction.

The driver's explanation that the trip simply ran long cannot justify the extra 3.20. On an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip POL-RD-11 fixes the distance and time charges at booking, so no amount of elapsed minutes or junction delay is chargeable to the rider over the quote; the driver's own submitted statement offers no figure the rider could be billed for.

The trace gives the driver no distance cover for the added charge either. EV-GPS-00524 records trace_distance_km 3.37 against an optimal 3.3 km — an excess of 0.07 km, or 2.12%, and the derived deviation status reads 'no deviation'. That is far below POL-RD-01's twin gates of 20% and 0.8 km, so the 3.20 is not a distance deviation that could be dressed up as extra driving; on this fare model it can only be the over-quote refundable under POL-RD-11(a).

The driver's assertion of 'some traffic at the last junction' is an uncited external-traffic excuse and it fails. Tested under POL-RD-13 against the traffic_advisory for this trip and nothing else, it cannot be run: EV-ADVIS-00524-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and no advisory covering the trip window is on file, so POL-RD-03 is unavailable and the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08. Because the driver names no advisory identifier, this is a gap in the bundle rather than a contradiction in it, and it is not a POL-RD-10(5) escalation trigger — the case remains one for a monetary ruling.

ledger.claim: The rider carries no heightened corroboration burden on this claim. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so POL-RD-08's special-corroboration trigger (4 or more claims with 1 or fewer substantiated) is not met, and the over-quote is established from the ledger itself rather than from any inference against the rider.

The 12.90 the rider says appeared once the dispute was raised is not reflected in the ledger, so the rider is still out of pocket and needs a ruling to move the money. EV-FARE-00524 shows payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00; under POL-GEN-03 that present state stands unless the tribunal orders otherwise, so a PARTIAL_REFUND of the 3.20 over-quote is what actually restores the quoted price to the rider.

POL-RD-01 sets a twin gate for this dispute and the rider fails both limbs. The governing trace figure — gps_trace.trace_distance_km of 3.37 km, which POL-RD-01 makes the ruling field and which the rounded trip_record copy of 3.4 km may NOT be used to test — exceeds the booked optimal of 3.3 km by only 0.07 km, an excess of 2.12%. Both sit far below the clause's 0.8 km absolute and 20% relative thresholds, so no route deviation is established on this trip's own evidence.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and must show, citing evidence, an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold measured from an unimpaired trace. She cannot: the clean trace records 0.07 km and 2.12% against a 0.8 km and 20% gate. The burden never shifts to the driver, and no exculpatory clause is needed because there is nothing to exculpate.

EV-GPS-00524 is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07. It carries 79 fixes at a 10-second cadence, coverage_pct 100.0, an empty gaps array and max_gap_sec 0.0, so none of limbs (a), (b) or (c) fires. The trace therefore decides the case at full weight and no POL-RD-10(3) escalation is engaged.

The fare_breakdown records fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE with quoted_fare_sgd 12.90, so POL-RD-02 does not run and under POL-RD-11 no distance-or-time refund is available to the rider however large the excess; the rider was already whole on distance and time at booking and the loss of any detour falls on the driver. The rider's own theory — that the fare rose because the trip 'took one minute longer' — is precisely the metered-duration complaint that POL-RD-11 forecloses.

A 2.12% excess is nowhere near the 50% 'material' line, so the POL-RD-06 driver_profile check is not even triggered. Were it consulted it clears the driver outright: deviation_flags_90d is 0 across 250 completed_trips_90d, no pattern under POL-RD-06 is established, and therefore no FULL_REFUND uplift and no driver-conduct referral follows.

There is no standalone correction to make under POL-RD-09. The ledger carries no ERP lines (erp_gantries empty, tolls_erp 0.00), no airport surcharge and waiting_time_fee 0.00, so there is no phantom gantry and no wrongly applied surcharge to refund. Nothing on this fare can be enlarged past POL-RD-11(a)'s quoted-versus-charged arithmetic by a pass-through correction.

No POL-RD-10 trigger fires and the case is rulable. The same trip_id TRP-00524 appears on the trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown; the pickup timestamps agree; the trace is unimpaired under POL-RD-07 so limb (3) is not met; and the computed move is nowhere near the SGD 150.00 ceiling in limb (6). Escalation, which is terminal and would hold the money, is not available on this record.

The driver's counterparty_statement refers to 'some traffic at the last junction' but names no advisory, and the traffic_advisory EV-ADVIS-00524-01 is MISSING — admissibility status MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT — so that artifact carries no fact and I disclose the impairment. Under POL-RD-13 an uncited traffic excuse is tested against nothing, carries no weight under POL-RD-08, and because no advisory identifier is cited the gap is not the exculpatory-clause-against-a-cited-artifact contradiction that POL-RD-10(5) escalates. In any event POL-RD-01 shows only 0.07 km of excess, so no exoneration was ever required.

On this rider-filed dispute the charge still stands — payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00. The deviation theory fails on the trace's own figures and POL-RD-11 closes the distance-and-time lines on an upfront-quoted trip, so the present payment state should be left intact and the outcome on the rider's claim is NO_ACTION.
